title: PIP-on-a-chip: A Label-free Study of Protein-phosphoinositide Interactions
protocol: Dilute 7x Cleaning Solution 7-fold with deionized water.
Heat the diluted cleaning solution to 95 °C for 20 min or until clear.
Arrange coverslips on an aluminum staining rack in alternating directions, leaving space between each cover slip.
Submerge the staining rack with coverslips in the cleaning solution.
Keep coverslips in the solution for 1 h, replenishing deionized water as needed to maintain concentration.
Wash coverslips extensively with deionized water to remove detergent.
Dry coverslips using nitrogen gas for approximately 5 min per staining rack.
Place dried coverslips in a kiln and anneal at 550 °C for 6 h.
Mix polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) prepolymer and curing agent at a 10:1 weight ratio in a large plastic weigh boat.
Degas the mixture in vacuum for 1 hour with vacuum strength of 500 Torr or less.
Place silicon master containing SU-8 micropatterns in a large plastic weigh boat.
Pour degassed PDMS into the weigh boat containing the silicon master.
Cure the PDMS in a dry oven at 60 °C overnight.
Gently peel off the PDMS from the silicon master with hands.
Mark the boundaries of each micropattern in rectangles using a surgical scalpel and ruler.
Cut the PDMS into blocks.
Punch 16 holes (8 inlets and 8 outlets per block) at both ends of each microchannel with a biopsy punch (1.0 mm hole diameter).
Apply tape over each PDMS block to protect micropatterns from damage and dust.
Store PDMS blocks in a plastic container.
Calculate the volume of POPC, PI(4,5)P2, and oSRB-POPE needed for SUV preparation.
Pipette 2.22 mg of POPC into a single 20 mL glass scintillation vial.
Add 0.26 mg of PI(4,5)P2 to the vial containing POPC.
Add 2.1 x 10^-5 mg of oSRB-POPE to the mixture in the vial.
Wet pipette tip with chloroform before use.
Dry the mixture in a stream of nitrogen gas for 10 min or until solvent evaporates.
Desiccate the dried lipid film under vacuum for ≥3 h at 10 mTorr.
Rehydrate the dried lipid film with 5 mL of running buffer (20 mM HEPES, 100 mM NaCl, pH 7.0).
Place rehydrated mixture in an ultrasonic bath operating at 35 kHz for 30 min at room temperature.
Freeze-thaw vesicle suspension with liquid nitrogen and water bath at 40 °C to get unilamellar vesicles.
Repeat freeze-thaw process 10 times.
Extrude the vesicle suspension through a 0.10 μm track-etched polycarbonate membrane using a lipid extruder.
Repeat the extrusion 10 times.
Test the inlets and outlets of the PDMS block for blockage by squirting deionized water through the holes using a water wash bottle.
Dry the PDMS block with nitrogen gas.
Place the PDMS block and pre-cleaned coverslip inside the oxygen plasma system sample chamber.
Expose the PDMS block and coverslip with oxygen plasma for 45 seconds at 75 Watts, 10 cm³/min oxygen flow speed, and 200 mTorr vacuum strength.
Contact the patterned surface of the PDMS block with the coverslip immediately after oxygen plasma treatment.
Press gently to remove any air bubbles at contact sites.
Place the device on a level hot plate at 100°C for 3 minutes to enhance bonding.
Use a wet lint-free wipe with 100% ethanol to remove dust particles from the top (PDMS) and bottom (glass) of the device.
Tape the device on top of a glass microscope slide.
Transfer 100 µL of PI(4,5)P2-containing SUVs into a 0.65 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Adjust the pH of the solution to ~3.2 by adding 6.4 µL of 0.2 N hydrochloric acid.
Pipette 10 µL of the pH-adjusted SUV solution into each channel through the inlet.
Apply pressure through the pipette until the solution reaches the outlet.
Detach the tip from the pipette and leave it attached to the device.
Repeat the above step for each channel.
Incubate the device for 10 min at RT.
Cut sets of inlet and outlet tubing, 60 cm (inlet) and 8 cm (outlet) long respectively.
Connect the outlet tubing set to the device using tweezers.
Tape the device onto a microscope stage.
Submerge one end of the inlet tubing set in 25 mL of running buffer contained in a conical tube.
Secure the tubing with tape.
Place the conical tube on a higher ground (~20 cm) than the device to push the solution through the microchannels via gravity flow.
For each inlet tube, use a syringe to draw 1 mL of running buffer from the free end of the tubing.
Remove the pipette tip from the inlet and insert the free end of the inlet tubing into the device.
Introduce a drop of running buffer onto the inlet.
Use a lint-free wipe to remove excess buffer after attaching inlet tubing to the device.
Repeat the step to connect all inlet tubing pieces to the device.
Flow running buffer through the channels to remove excess vesicles and equilibrate the bilayer.
Open the microscope control software (see table of materials).
Click on the "Microscope" tab and choose the "10X" objective.
Click on "Live" and then "Alexa 568" image icons on the toolbar.
Focus on the microchannels using fine and course adjustment knobs.
Scan through the device to check the quality of SLBs and channels.
Click "FL Shutter Closed" image icon on the toolbar.
Click on the "Acquisition" tab, and under "Basic adjustments," select "Exposure time."
Set the exposure time to "200 ms".
Under the filters menu, select the red channel (marked as "Alexa 568").
Set the time interval to 5 min, duration to 30 min in the "time lapse" menu.
Click "Start".
Select the "Circle" tool under the "Measure" tab.
Draw a circle in any channel.
Right click while the circle is selected and choose "Properties".
Under the "Profile" tab, check "all T" to view the fluorescence intensity as a function of time.
Ensure this curve reaches a plateau indicating equilibrium before proceeding.
Lower the buffer solution to an equal ground level as the device to stop the flow.
Save the time lapse file.
Prepare dilutions of the PH domain using the running buffer as a diluent.
Use at least two channels for blank controls, placing them at the far ends on each side.
Apply 200 µL of each protein dilution into the outlet channel using a pipette.
Do not apply pressure; let gravity do the work.
Detach the tip from the pipette and leave it attached to the microfluidic device.
Repeat the above step for each channel, ensuring no air bubbles are introduced.
Lower the inlet tubing to a ground below the microfluidic device.
Tape the free end of the tubing to a waste container.
Flow protein dilutions for 30 min.
Click on "Start" under the "Time Lapse" tab in the software to begin imaging again.
Repeat step 5.15 to ensure equilibrium is reached.
Save the time lapse file when the experiment is complete.
Follow the procedure for cleaning glass coverslips as previously described.
Fabricate micropatterned PDMS blocks as previously described.
Prepare SUVs as previously described.
Assemble the microfluidic device as previously described.
Form SLBs as previously described.
Focus the microscope on the bilayer.
Set the exposure time to 200 ms and the binning to 1.
Photo-bleach a circular spot using a 532 nm, 2 mW laser beam (13 µM radius).
Immediately after photobleaching, start capturing images every 3 s for the first 45 s.
Capture images at 30 s intervals for the remainder of the time (total duration of 15 min).
Save the time lapse file upon completion of data acquisition.
Select the bleached area using the circle drawing tool to extract fluorescence intensity values as a function of time.
Select an unbleached region nearby and another area without any SLBs.
Calculate the fluorescence recovery using the equation Ft / Fi - F0.
Plot fluorescence recovery (y-axis) against time (x-axis) to generate a FRAP curve.
Fit the data to a single exponential function.
Determine the mobile fraction (A) and kinetic constant (k).
Calculate the half-time to recovery (t1/2) using the equation ln(2)/k.
Open the time lapse files of before and after titrating the PH domain.
Go to the last frame of each time lapse file.
Do a line scan across all microchannels to obtain fluorescence intensity data as a function of distance in pixels.
Transfer the data to a spreadsheet software.
Sample some data within the channel and either side of the channel representing the baseline for normalization.
Normalize the data to the blank channel using the provided formula.
